title: SPA/303/2014 of Uttarakhand Public Service Commission Vs Rahul Ruhela AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 303 of 2014
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission Ö...Appellant.
Versus
Rahul Ruhela and others ÖÖ Respondents.
Present:
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. H.M. Bhatia, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for respondent No. 1.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Honíble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Honíble Alok Singh, J.
Dated: 16th June, 2017
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)

This appeal, maintained by the Uttarakhand Public
Service Commission, is directed against the judgment passed
by the learned Single Judge by which the writ petition has
been allowed.
2. The writ petitioner was a candidate in the selection for
the post of Junior Engineer (Agriculture Engineering) in the
Minor Irrigation Department, Government of Uttarakhand.
He challenged the selection process on the basis that it is in
violation of the Rules. It would appear that the writ
petitioner, respondent Nos. 4 and 5 scored the same
aggregate marks, namely, 203. The respondent No. 5 scored
the highest marks in the written examination, i.e. 173,
followed by the petitioner and 4th respondent who scored
171 and 166 marks respectively. The learned Single Judge
found that even though all the three scored equal aggregate
marks but respondent No. 5 scored highest marks in the

written examination. What applies would appear to be Rule
15 (6) of the Uttaranchal Service of Junior Engineers (Group
ëCí) Minor Irrigation (Irrigation Department) Rules, 2003
which provides that if two or more candidates obtained
equal marks in the aggregate, the name of the candidate
obtaining higher marks in the written examination shall be
placed higher in the list. The learned Single Judge noted that
the 5th respondent was already given appointment. In terms
of the said same Rule, it was found that petitioner must be
given preference over the 4th respondent as he secured
higher marks in the written examination. The Court further
proceeded to note that there was one seat vacant. It was
noted that it is actually earmarked for the physically
challenged person. Paragraph 8, 9 and 10 of the judgment
are extracted hereunder :
ì8. The procedure for determining the vacancies
for physically challenged persons is given in the U.P.
Public Services (Reservation for Physically
Handicapped, Dependants of Freedom-fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Act, 1993 (from hereinafter referred to as
ìthe Act of 1993î). Section 3 of the Act of 1993, reserves
certain vacancies for physically challenged persons but
such vacancies should be earmarked and it must be
notified by the State Government under Section 3 (1) (ii)
of the Act of 1993. Section 3 of the Act of 1993 reads as
under:-
ì3. Reservation of vacancies in favour of
physically handicapped etc.- (1) There shall be
reserved at the stage of direct recruitment-
(i) ÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖ
(i-a) ÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖÖ.
(ii) in such public services and posts as the State
Government may, by notification, identify on per cent
of vacancies each for the persons suffering from, -
 (a) blindness or low vision;
 (b) hearing impairment; and
 (c) locomotor disability or cerebral palsy.î

9. On the last occasion, since this was the
question while hearing the matter, this Court had
passed following order:-
 ìAfter hearing the learned counsel for the
parties, it transpires that one post of Junior
Engineer in Minor Irrigation Department which
was reserved for Physically challenged
candidate has been carried forward in view of
Section 3 (5) of the U.P. Public Services
(Reservation for Physically Handicapped,
Dependants of Freedom-fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Act, 1993.
Let an affidavit be filed by the
State/respondent nos. 1 & 2 to the effect as to
whether the vacancy was notified under Section
3 (1) (ii) of the U.P. Public Services (Reservation
for Physically Handicapped, Dependants of
Freedom-fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Act, 1993
or not?
Learned counsel for the State undertakes
to file an affidavit to this effect at the earliest
preferably within two weeks.
List this matter on 5th May, 2014 in daily
cause list.î
10. Today, a supplementary counter affidavit
has been filed on behalf of respondent no.3, wherein it
has been stated that the Secretary to the Government
of Uttarakhand vide letter dated 20th November,
2012, which is annexed as Annexure No.2 to the
supplementary counter affidavit, has admitted that in
the Minor Irrigation Department though no post has
been notified/earmarked under Section 3 (1) (ii) of the
Act of 1993, but since reservation has to be made for
physically challenged persons one post for hearing
impairment has been reserved in Minor Irrigation
Department.î
3. The learned Single Judge took the view that vacancy
was wrongly carried forward as the vacancy has not been
notified for the physically disabled person. On the basis of
this, the learned Single Judge took the view that
appointment letter may be issued to the 4th respondent on

the additional vacancy reserved wrongly for the physically
challenged person. The writ petition was allowed. The
petitioner was declared selected and directed to be given
letter of appointment. The 4th respondent was also directed
to be accommodated in the vacancy which was wrongly
earmarked and carried forward for the physically challenged
person. It is this judgment which is challenged before us by
the Public Service Commission.
4. We heard Mr. B.D. Kandpal, learned counsel for the
appellant, Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for respondent No.
1 and Mr. H.M. Bhatia, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
5. In fact, there is no dispute that Government of
Uttarakhand has accepted the impugned judgment. We are
of the view that the appellant has not been able to make out
any case for interference. We affirm the judgment of the
learned Single Judge. The appeal is dismissed. No order as
to costs.
(Alok Singh, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C. J.)
 16.06.2017 16.06.2017
